_comment: Thickness is metres of material represented by a full block (est.), multiplied once by the path inside the collision shape. Unlisted thickness is 1.0. Natural soil/rock/ores, terracotta and logs remain solid metres. Smooth/polished stone, quartz and prismarine have no unambiguous wall/board interpretation, so retain 1.0. Existing kind/S/breach values are preserved; new shape entries retain the previous bomb fallback ROCK/S=1.

_sources.stone_wall: (est.) Stone masonry wall: 0.40 m, within the 350–450 mm range in Nepal NBC 203, table 7.1(b): https://giwmscdnone.gov.np/media/pdf_upload/low-strength-masonry_mwykate.pdf
_sources.concrete_element: (est.) Concrete wall/floor element: 0.20 m, rounded 8 inches; HUD Residential Structural Design Guide (2nd ed.), sec. 4.3, typical 6/8/10-inch walls: https://www.govinfo.gov/content/pkg/GOVPUB-HH14-PURL-gpo86806/pdf/GOVPUB-HH14-PURL-gpo86806.pdf
_sources.brick_wall: (est.) Residential masonry wall: 0.38 m; 380 mm example: https://www.wienerberger.ua/produkciya/porotherm-glinyana-cegla/katalog-blokiv-porotherm/porotherm-38-p_w.html . The block analogy does not model cavities.
_sources.timber_boarding: (est.) Boarded timber element: 0.04 m per full block; a half slab represents 0.02 m. USDA FPL-GTR-190 (2010), ch. 17, 19 mm boards and 38 mm framing: https://research.fs.usda.gov/treesearch/37440
_sources.timber_panel: (est.) 3/16-block panel × 0.20 = 0.0375 m timber, approximately the 38 mm timber section in USDA FPL-GTR-190, ch. 17. Shape is counted once: https://research.fs.usda.gov/treesearch/37440
_sources.timber_frame: (est.) Quarter-block post × 0.16 = 0.04 m timber; 1/8-block rail = 0.02 m. Rounded 38/19 mm timber sections, USDA FPL-GTR-190, ch. 17: https://research.fs.usda.gov/treesearch/37440
